players.product: data center buildings owned and operated for GPU clusters (owner / operator of the Columbus, Georgia site hosting Axe Compute's B300 cluster)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Doug Recker / CFO Chris: Duos signed a 20-megawatt deal in the Carolinas with 'a very mature cloud provider, a public company, that is bankable' (not named), with deployment expected by the end of April 2027. CFO: 'it is a 10-year committed contract' at about $2.2 million of revenue per megawatt, 'just under half a billion dollars on its full run rate basis'; CEO: 'This is about a $450, $460 million' deal for over 10 years (CFO: '460, yeah'), with more 5-20 MW deployments possible with this customer.
quarterly_data.figure: 20 MW; about $460 million over 10 years; deployment by the end of April 2027

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Doug Recker on capacity: Columbus is billing 7 MW now and is being upgraded to 10 MW for the hyperscaler; Duos signed a contract and is deploying a 4 MW customer, a well-backed neocloud, in Roberta, Georgia; the day's press release says Duos has secured over 100 megawatt of land and power across the country, and it has identified over 100 MW of 5-20 MW tranches deliverable within 60-90 days. Duos has a backlog of 'probably over 20 plus customers' and is choosing among them on creditworthiness.
quarterly_data.figure: Columbus billing 7 MW (upgrading to 10 MW); Roberta, Georgia 4 MW; over 100 megawatt of land and power secured

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Doug Recker / CFO Chris on build model and unit economics: Duos deploys at around $6 million-$6.5 million a megawatt (with land) versus the $12 million-$14 million the large builders use (as spoken; the same-day 8-K investor deck prints a different industry-standard range), because its E-House (UPS, switchgear, main transformers) is built off-site and Trane builds its closed-loop chiller plant; it can build a 1 MW or 20 MW facility in under six months and parallel 1 MW generators to 10 MW in under four months. It charges about $180 per kW (as spoken; the same-day 8-K investor deck prints a different contracted rate) with power passed through at cost, on fixed-price 5- to 10-year terms, and does not own the GPUs. Payback (CFO / CEO): under three years for its 4 MW sites and a little under five years for the larger ones.
quarterly_data.figure: $6 million-$6.5 million per MW; about $180 per kW; payback under three years (4 MW sites) to a little under five years (larger sites)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Doug Recker on the infrastructure (Technology Solutions) division: Duos buys direct from Schneider, Vertiv, Eaton and Corning, avoiding a 30% markup; the division, which has four people (hires with long distribution experience), sells to colocation operators and hyperscalers at a 12%-15% average margin and, he believes, has done almost $30 million year to date.
quarterly_data.figure: almost $30 million year to date; 12%-15% margin

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Doug Recker on the market: a tier 1 customer signed 80 plus colo agreements last year and only 3 came to fruition because the power did not come up; Duos goes only where power is already there (transformers usually already on the property). GPU clusters used to be a megawatt and customers now look at 4.5 megawatt clusters; Duos has been a pure colocation business since August (CFO).

connects_to.relationship: data center capacity (owned and operated buildings) for Axe Compute GPU clusters

contracts.signal: CEO Doug Recker: Duos just deployed its first cluster with Axe Compute, which has a tier 1 hyperscaler customer - 4.7 megawatt in under 75 days, with Supermicro delivering the product; the 55 MW deal with Axe Compute is two different sites, a 35 and a 20 MW site, going in Ohio, Carolinas, Oregon, with a tier 1 hyperscaler behind Axe Compute.
contracts.units: 4.7 megawatt deployed in under 75 days; 55 MW (35 MW and 20 MW sites)
